# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 84 (Bi-Vb Pc84)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc84  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 84  
**Title (English, from literature):** Using sunshades and sandals  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chattupāhana-sikkhāpada* ("Rule on Sunshades and Sandals") is the eighty-fourth pācittiya rule of the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a nun who uses both a sunshade (*chatta*) and sandals (*upāhanā*) incurs an offense that must be confessed. In the word commentary (*padabhājanīya*), an exception is made for a nun who is ill (*gilānā*), defined as one who is not comfortable without a sunshade and sandals, whereas one who is healthy (*agilānā*) is comfortable without them [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary further specifies three types of sunshade—white cloth (*setacchatta*), rush matting (*kilañjacchatta*), and leaf (*paṇṇacchatta*)—constructed with circular bindings (*maṇḍalabaddha*) and ribs (*salākabaddha*), while *upāhanā* is left unglossed, as discussed also in the *Samantapāsādikā* in relation to Sekhiya 57 [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels for the rule are widespread across early Buddhist Vinaya lineages. Parallels exist in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (Pācittiya 84), as well as in the Dharmaguptaka (*pācittiya* 158), Mahīśāsaka (*pācittiya* 142/157), Sarvāstivāda (*pācittiya* 148/149), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Tibetan and Chinese *pācittiya* 131), Mahāsaṅghika (*pācittiya* 112), and the Sanskrit Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga (*pācittiya* 112). An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
